sentences.text:
By order dated 10.01.2025, the Ld. JMFC (Mahila Court)01, West, found that based on the police report in case FIR No. 395/2021, PS Kirti Nagar, the four accuseds - Sudarshan, Govinda,
Kavita and Vicky must be charged for having committed offences punishable u/sec. 498A/406 r/w 34 IPC.
Two of these accuseds i.e. Govinda and Sudarshan have preferred the present revision petitions against order dated 10.01.2025 of Ld. JMFC.
By the said revision petitions, the petitioners pray that the impugned order dated 10.01.2025 be set aside in respect of the petitioners - Govinda and Sudarshan.
2. It is argued by Ld. counsel for the petitioners that the material before the Ld. Magistrate was not sufficient enough to charge the petitioners for the offences as they were charged.

Upon inquiry from the Ld. counsel for the petitioners, it is discovered that they had not moved any application in writing seeking discharge CR No. 116/2025 : Govinda vs. State nor had they presented written arguments to the Ld. Magistrate justifying their claim to be discharged.

3. Before the trial court, the petitioners had argued that in view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India made in Crl. Appeal No. 195/2022, titled Kahkashan Kausar @ Sonam &
Ors. vs. State of Bihar & Ors., the petitioners i.e. Sudarshan and Govinda must be discharged.

Ors. vs. State of Bihar & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4. Same is the crux of arguments made by the Ld. counsel for the petitioners in the present petition as he asserts that the allegations against the petitioners are vague and general and therefore, the petitioners could not have been charged on general allegations.

5. Ld. counsel for the petitioners cite para 9 of the above referred judgment wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has held that where the allegations made against any person are general and omnibus, their prosecution on such allegations is unwarranted.
Para 19 of said judgment is reproduced below :
"Coming to the facts of this case, upon a perusal of the contents of the FIR dated 01.04.2019, it is revealed that general allegations are levelled against the Appellants.
The complainant alleged that 'all accused harassed her mentally and threatened her of terminating her pregnancy'.

Furthermore, no specific and distinct allegations have been made against either of the Appellants herein, i.e., none of the Appellants have been attributed any specific role in furtherance of the general allegations made against them.
This simply leads to a CR No. 116/2025 : Govinda vs. State situation wherein one fails to ascertain the role played by each accused in furtherance of the offence.
The allegations are therefore general and omnibus and can at best be said to have been made out on account of small skirmishes.

Insofar as husband is concerned,
since he has not appealed against the order of the High Court, we have not examined the veracity of allegations made against him.
However, as far as the Appellants are concerned, the allegations made against them being general and omnibus, do not warrant prosecution."

6. If the present case is analyzed in line with the above quoted para relied upon by the revisionists, it is found that in the complaint, which is the starting point of the proceedings in which the impugned Sudarshan vs State on 8 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137757124/
2 order is made, specific allegations against petitioner Govinda, who is brotherinlaw of the complainant are levelled and specific incident has been identified by the complainant in space and time i.e. in the night of 13.04.2017, when the complainant was sleeping with her husband, petitioner - Govinda had made unwarranted, unsolicited sexual advances towards the complainant.

sentences.text: The complaint also contains specific allegations against petitioner Sudarshan, who is fatherinlaw of the complainant.
The specific allegations are that he took her to a Tantrik and forced her to consume illicit substance, which used to affect her orientation and consciousness.

The Ld. Magistrate while ordering the framing of charge against the petitioners, by impugned order, had recorded the finding that specific allegations against all the four accuseds were present in the narrative of the complainant but the Ld. Magistrate CR No. 116/2025 : Govinda vs. State had not cited them specifically.

The impugned order does not warrant to be interfered with only because the Ld.
Magistrate had not cited the specific allegations.
The findings of the Ld. Magistrate does not deserve to be interfered with.
Revision petitions are dismissed.
7. Trial court record along with an attested copy of this order be sent back to trial court.
8. Revision petition files be consigned to Record Room.
